channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Former ‘Hard Fork’ Hosts in Talks for Seven-Figure Podcast Deal
item.description: As wealthy tech companies scramble to reach early adopters, two tech podcasters are nearing a deal that could be worth up to $5 million a year
item.dc:creator: Ashley Carman

item.title: Duo Will Make Up 10% of All iPhone Sales, Munster Says
item.description: Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner and co-founder Gene Munster says Apple's foldable iPhone Duo will eventually make up 10% of all iPhone sales. He says the higher price point won't keep customers away. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Touts Cybersecurity as Next Big Market for AI
item.description: Cybersecurity is the next big market for artificial intelligence, with advances in the technology set to disrupt an industry geared to defending computer systems, said Nvidia Corp. co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Everything You Need to Know About Apple's iPhone Duo
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow discusses Apple's iPhone Duo with Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, from its anticipated reception with consumers to what it means for Apple's new era under CEO John Ternus. Plus, the AI chip race is moving to inference. And, Elon Musk's Boring Co. reaches a $23 billion valuation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazilian ID-Verification Firm Unico Acquires Argentina’s Valida
item.description: Brazilian identity verification company Unico agreed to acquire an Argentine competitor as part of its broader expansion in Latin America.
item.dc:creator: Mie Dahl

item.title: Moonshot Secretly Routed User Requests Through Claude, Anthropic Says
item.description: Anthropic PBC accused China’s artificial intelligence champion Moonshot AI of covertly routing thousands of user requests to the US firm’s Claude models and passing off the responses as its own in a bid to gain an edge in the AI race.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz, Maggie Eastland and Jordan Robertson

item.title: Musk’s Boring Co. Gets $23 Billion Valuation
item.description: Elon Musk's Boring Co. secured $3 billion in fresh investment backed by the United Arab Emirates and affiliated entities, in a funding round valuing Elon Musk’s tunneling startup at $23 billion. Bloomberg's Kiel Porter has the details and joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: BofA: Apple’s Ternus Era Starts With Innovation, AI
item.description: Bank of America says John Ternus’s first major product launch as Apple CEO reinforced the company’s focus on product innovation, privacy and increasingly personalized AI. Wamsi Mohan, managing director and senior equity research analyst at Bank of America sees the new foldable iPhone Duo expanding Apple’s addressable market, while on-device AI and Private Cloud Compute could make Siri more capable without sacrificing user privacy. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech."Bank of America says John Ternus’s first major product launch as Apple CEO reinforced the company’s focus on product innovation, privacy and increasingly personalized AI. Wamsi Mohan, managing director and senior equity research analyst at Bank of America sees the new foldable iPhone Duo expanding Apple’s addressable market, while on-device AI and Private Cloud Compute could make Siri more capable without sacrificing user privacy. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: d-Matrix Joins Nvidia’s AI Inference Push
item.description: Nvidia is embracing the rise of custom AI chips as demand shifts toward specialized systems built for inference. d-Matrix CEO Sid Sheth discusses the startup’s new partnership with Nvidia, which will integrate its inference-focused XPUs with Nvidia GPUs using NVLink Fusion, and why inference is emerging as the next major battleground in AI compute. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Breaking Down Apple's First Foldable iPhone With Mark Gurman
item.description: Apple unveiled the company’s first foldable smartphone during a wide-ranging event Wednesday, betting that a new category can energize growth for its best-selling lineup. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech" to break it all down. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Surges Above $105, Arnott Warns of Bubble Risk
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Oil above $105. Stocks and Treasuries sinking as rate-hike bets build. Plus, housing hits a fresh slowdown, Macy’s disappoints, and Rob Arnott warns markets look frothy. And Joe Kaiser joins us on the next phase of the AI boom where power may become the biggest constraint. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Next Phase of the AI Boom
item.description: The AI boom is entering a new phase, where electricity could become the biggest constraint. Switchyard Partners CEO Joe Kaiser joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why data centers may increasingly move to stranded power, why capitalism could produce better AI guardrails and why dramatically lowering compute per task will be key to sustaining the next wave of AI investment. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top Pentagon Official Rejects Anthropic Researcher’s AI Warning
item.description: A top Pentagon official is pushing back against rising fears about artificial intelligence risks days after a public warning from an Anthropic PBC engineer that AI insiders believe the technology “could kill us all by the end of the decade.”
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride

item.title: Saudis Weigh Merging EA With Savvy to Create Global Gaming Giant
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s wealth fund is considering combining Electronic Arts Inc. with Savvy Games, people familiar with the matter said, in a deal that would bring blockbuster titles like Madden NFL and Pokemon Go under one roof.
item.dc:creator: Dinesh Nair and Cecilia D'Anastasio

item.title: BNP Says Too Much AI Borrowing Will End Bull Market in Credit
item.description: The breaking of the years-long rally in corporate bonds will happen when technology companies saturate markets with too much debt, according to a prediction from BNP Paribas SA.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Martin

item.title: Robotics Startup Skild AI Hits $100 Million in Revenue Run Rate
item.description: Skild AI Inc., a fast-growing startup that develops software to help robots learn tasks, has reached $100 million in recurring revenue run-rate, 10 months after beginning commercial use.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Kelly

item.title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo Is Here, What We Know
item.description: Apple unveiled the company’s first foldable smartphone during a wide-ranging event Wednesday, betting that a new category can energize growth for its biggest-selling lineup. The iPhone Duo will start at $1,999 and cost up to $3,199. This was the first product reveal event for the new CEO John Ternus. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow was there and reports from Apple Park in Cupertino, California. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Gives US Agencies 50% Off Models, Ending $1 Per Year Deal
item.description: OpenAI is ending a pilot program that allowed government agencies to use its models for only $1 per year and moving to a usage-based pricing system that will give federal workers access to the technology at a 50% discount from standard prices, according to a statement from the General Services Administration.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Snap Launches Planning Feature to Make Meet-Ups With Friends
item.description: Snap Inc. launched new event-planning features enabling Snapchat users to organize gatherings with friends, send invitations and collect responses without leaving the app.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra S. Levine

item.title: DeepSeek’s Low-Cost Model Deals a Fresh Blow to OpenAI, Z.AI
item.description: DeepSeek rolled out an AI model that charges as little as a fraction of a cent per million tokens, ramping up the pressure on rivals from Anthropic PBC to Z.AI Co.
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai
